instruction: I keep visiting this Wikipedia page. Can you add a desktop shortcut for quick access using Chrome's shortcut creation feature?

metadata.explanation: Task asks user to create a desktop shortcut for Wikipedia AI page using Chrome's built-in shortcut feature. The evaluator checks for a .desktop file on the desktop with the correct Name field matching 'Artificial intelligence - Wikipedia'. Using name-based matching is more reliable than app-id based matching since Chrome-generated app-ids are environment-dependent.
metadata.verification: Reused existing is_shortcut_on_desktop metric and shortcuts_on_desktop getter. Changed from type='exec' (which requires environment-specific app-id) to type='name' which matches the shortcut name 'Artificial intelligence - Wikipedia' - a more stable and environment-agnostic approach.

llm_judge_reasons: Evaluator logic semantically correct: checks desktop for .desktop file with Name field matching 'Artificial intelligence - Wikipedia'
Getter (shortcuts_on_desktop) correctly extracts desktop shortcut files and their contents from filesystem (chrome.py:1084-1116)
Metric (is_shortcut_on_desktop) correctly searches for 'Name=<expected_name>\n' in .desktop file content when type='name' (chrome.py:492-495)
Expected value 'Artificial intelligence - Wikipedia' semantically correct - matches actual Wikipedia page title from URL https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Artificial_intelligence
Complete coverage: evaluator verifies the core requirement that desktop shortcut was created with correct name
Data flow correct: getter returns {path: file_content}, metric searches for Name field in content
No postconfig needed: .desktop files are persistent file artifacts on disk, not transient UI state - getter reads from filesystem not UI
Static warning is false positive: unlike print dialogs or settings windows, desktop shortcuts persist as files after creation
